chunks: What al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān narrated from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who pledged collateral until a specified time, then disappeared: is there a time at which his collateral may be sold? He said: “No, not until he comes.”

key_terms.رَهَنَ: to pledge or place property as collateral
key_terms.رَهْنًا: a pledge or collateral held as security
key_terms.وَقْتٍ: a specified term or time limit

ai.seo_question: Can pledged collateral be sold if the debtor disappears before returning?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on pledged collateral (rahn) when its owner disappears after setting a term. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام rules that the pledged property is not to be sold until the owner returns, indicating protection of property rights in such a case.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4106 - Al-Qasim ibn Sulaiman narrated from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who reported from Abu Abdullah (as) regarding a man who pledged a security (rahn) for a specified time and then disappeared, should there be a time set to sell his pledge?"
Imam (as) replied: "No, it should not be sold until he returns."
